title: Failure Storyboard + Retry Heuristics Prototype
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Operators and engineers using Redwood Console have trouble triaging intermittent failed requests that involve retries across multiple backend variants. Context: existing failure views are event-centric and do not surface the narrative of how a request evolved (initial failure, retry attempts, model variant fallback, KV cache misses) or the heuristic signals that indicate a retry is likely to succeed. Goal: create a lightweight storyboard UI that stitches timeline, payload diffs, error taxonomy hints, and a retry-heuristics panel so that engineers can rapidly decide next steps (investigate payload, open rollout, or escalate to infra). This ticket produces an interactive prototype, acceptance criteria, and a short usability script for SRE/PM review.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive Figma prototype demonstrates: timeline view with grouped retry attempts, inline payload diff for the initial and final attempt, and a retry-heuristics card that lists likely causes and suggested actions.
Prototype includes an explicit mapping from observed error classes (e.g., kernel OOM, KV cache miss, model tokenization error, downstream 5xx) to suggested remediation steps and confidence scores.
Design review signoff from PM (Priya Nair) and an engineering feasibility note (ENG-assign) attached in comments.
Usability test run with at least 4 SRE/ML engineers using the provided script; summarize results in attachments.
Design assets (Figma frames + exportable tokens) uploaded to the Console design library and linked from this ticket.
tasks: Draft storyboard flows and identify 3 canonical failure scenarios (cache miss, model fallback, infra transient).
Build interactive Figma prototype (desktop modal + details pane).
Create payload diff visual component spec (line-level diffs for JSON payloads).
Design retry-heuristics card with ranked cause hypotheses and quick actions (Retry, Open Rollout, Escalate).
Run 4 moderated usability sessions and collect feedback notes.
Incorporate engineering feedback about telemetry gaps and update acceptance criteria.
comments: 2025-02-11 Tomas Rivera: Kicked off initial discovery. Pulled logs sample for three tenants (internal-prod, beta-customer). Observed that many retries are identical payloads with different model variants — we'll surface variant lineage.

2025-02-18 Priya Nair (PM): Suggested we prioritize the payload diff and suggested-actions card—these are highest ROI for first-release. Also asked to surface cost impact of retries in the card as an optional metric.

2025-02-22 Eng feedback - Jordan Blake: Feasibility note: payload diffs are fine but line-level diffs must be computed server-side for large requests. Need an API that returns 'delta tokens' and a render token to avoid client parsing overhead. Added dependency ENG-9174.

2025-02-26 Aisha Kapoor: Uploaded first Figma prototype link and test script. Waiting on engineering to confirm telemetry (has_kv_cache_hit, variant_id, retry_reason) availability. See design_links for files.

2025-03-02 Usability run summary: 4 engineers. Key findings: a) users loved the storyboard narrative card, b) some confusion about suggested-action confidence score terminology — changed to 'confidence band' and added tooltip, c) requested quick-copy links to open a filtered console page for the failing model variant. Updated mockups accordingly.
decisions: Render payload diffs as a compressed summary by default with an expand option to view full token-level diff (decision: reduce cognitive load for long payloads).
Show retry cost estimate (approx tokens x token_cost) as an optional metric — will be gated behind a toggle in Console settings to avoid noise for first-time users.
Map error classes to suggested actions; confidence is derived from a heuristic score using occurrence frequency and recent success rate of retries.
blockers: Telemetry gap: ENG-9174 must add delta-token API (see comment).
Access control question: for private deployments we need to verify that payload diffs don't violate logging redaction policies (security to confirm).
